blocks.content: Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 specifies the duties, powers, and functions of the Authority to protect the interests of policyholders and regulate the insurance sector.

items: Malhotra Committee (1994) laid the foundation for setting up IRDAI as an autonomous regulatory body.
IRDAI headquarters were relocated from Delhi to Hyderabad in 2002.
The 10-member IRDAI body includes 1 Chairman, up to 5 full-time members, and up to 4 part-time members.
Maintenance of minimum solvency margin by insurance firms is strictly monitored under IRDAI powers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI was established under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 following recommendations of the Malhotra Committee.
Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999 lays down all duties, powers, and functions of the regulatory authority.
IRDAI holds the authority to issue, modify, renew, suspend, or cancel registration certificates of insurers.
It mandates solvency margin levels and controls how insurance companies invest their assets and funds.
The authority specifies mandatory codes of conduct and qualifications for agents, intermediaries, and loss assessors.
